LESSON: THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF LIFE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living things and their Environment
Topic 2.4: The Interdependence of Life

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Interdependence of Life. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the role of living and non-living factors in environments?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment
2. construct food chains and food webs in the environment
3. describe the effect of human activities on the environment
4. appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF LIFE
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Interdependence of Life helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF LIFE
Study The Interdependence of Life like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “The Interdependence of Life” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct food chains and food webs in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to construct food chains and food webs in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct food chains and food webs in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why The Interdependence of Life matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct food chains and food webs in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the effect of human activities on the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the effect of human activities on the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the effect of human activities on the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to The Interdependence of Life this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the effect of human activities on the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “The Interdependence of Life” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Interdependence of Life is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “The Interdependence of Life” around your school. (skill: explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment)

Example 2: Say why The Interdependence of Life matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: construct food chains and food webs in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to The Interdependence of Life this week. (skill: describe the effect of human activities on the environment)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “The Interdependence of Life” around your school. (skill: appreciate the interdependence between living and non-living factors of the environment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Interdependence of Life to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment.
3. Practise this skill: construct food chains and food webs in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: describe the effect of human activities on the environment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of The Interdependence of Life from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Interdependence of Life: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study The Interdependence of Life?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the role of living and non-living factors in environments?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Interdependence of Life means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the biotic and abiotic factors of the environment.
5. Be able to: construct food chains and food webs in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
